security_hardening.title: Add SSRF Protection for External Image URL Processing
security_hardening.description: Multiple AI routes (/image/edit, /image/remove-bg, /image/upscale, /image/outpaint, /image/restore) accept user-provided image URLs and pass them directly to external APIs (Replicate, OpenRouter) without URL validation. The ensureDataUri helper only checks if URLs start with 'http' or 'data:'. An attacker could provide internal URLs (e.g., http://localhost, http://169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata) to perform Server-Side Request Forgery attacks.
security_hardening.rationale: SSRF vulnerabilities can expose internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (AWS/GCP credentials), and internal network resources. The AI proxy nature of the application makes this especially critical as it forwards requests to external services with server-side credentials.
security_hardening.currentRisk: Attacker can access internal services or cloud metadata endpoints by providing malicious URLs in image processing requests
security_hardening.remediation: Implement a URL validation middleware that: 1) Only allows HTTPS URLs, 2) Blocks private IP ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x, localhost, 127.x.x.x), 3) Blocks cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), 4) Optionally maintains an allowlist of trusted image domains (replicate.delivery, googleusercontent.com, etc.)

security_hardening.title: Implement Email Verification Enforcement Before Full Access
security_hardening.description: The authentication system sends verification emails but does not enforce verification before allowing full application access. Users can sign up with fake emails and immediately access all features including AI generation. The code contains a TODO note acknowledging this gap: 'TODO: Add email_verified boolean to users schema if strictly required.' (auth.ts line 239-241)
security_hardening.rationale: Without email verification enforcement, attackers can create unlimited accounts with fake emails for abuse (spam, quota exhaustion, ban evasion). This also affects compliance requirements that mandate verified contact information.
security_hardening.currentRisk: Users can access all application features without proving email ownership, enabling spam accounts, quota abuse, and ban evasion
security_hardening.remediation: 1) Add 'emailVerified' boolean column to users table with default false, 2) Update signup to set emailVerified=false, 3) Update verify-email endpoint to set emailVerified=true, 4) Add middleware that restricts AI/storage features to verified users, 5) Show verification reminder banner for unverified users

security_hardening.title: Add Session Regeneration After Authentication
security_hardening.description: The current login flow creates a new session (auth.ts line 168: 'lucia.createSession(user.id, {})') but does not explicitly invalidate any pre-existing session from the same request. If an attacker can set a session cookie before login (via XSS or other means), they could potentially exploit session fixation.
security_hardening.rationale: Session fixation is a well-known attack where attackers force victims to use a known session ID. While the Lucia auth library provides good defaults and the CSRF middleware helps, explicitly invalidating old sessions on login adds defense in depth.
security_hardening.currentRisk: Potential session hijacking if attacker can pre-set session cookies before user authentication
security_hardening.remediation: Before creating a new session on login, check for and invalidate any existing session for the current request: 1) Read existing sessionId from cookie, 2) If exists, call lucia.invalidateSession(existingSessionId), 3) Then proceed with lucia.createSession(). This ensures any pre-set session is destroyed.

security_hardening.title: Remove Sensitive Debug Logging from Production Code
security_hardening.description: Several files contain console.log statements that could leak sensitive information in production logs: server/check_token.ts logs verification tokens (line 13), server/probe_replicate.ts logs API key existence and length (lines 5-6), vite.config.ts logs token presence details (lines 31, 37, 41). While not logging full secrets, this metadata aids reconnaissance.
security_hardening.rationale: Debug logging that references tokens, keys, or authentication data—even indirectly—provides information to attackers about what secrets exist and how they're used. In shared log aggregators (Datadog, CloudWatch), this data could be exposed to unauthorized parties.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
security_hardening.currentRisk: Log aggregation systems may expose API key metadata and token information to unauthorized parties
security_hardening.remediation: 1) Remove or gate debug logging behind NODE_ENV !== 'production', 2) Delete probe_*.ts files if they're only for debugging, 3) Replace direct token/key logging with boolean checks only (e.g., 'Has token: true'), 4) Add structured logging that explicitly excludes sensitive fields

security_hardening.title: Strengthen CSP with Report-URI for Security Monitoring
security_hardening.description: The Content-Security-Policy is well-configured (script-src 'self', no unsafe-eval) but lacks a report-uri or report-to directive. CSP violations—which could indicate XSS attempts or misconfigured resources—are not being monitored or logged. Adding CSP reporting enables proactive security monitoring.
security_hardening.rationale: CSP reporting provides visibility into potential XSS attempts and identifies legitimate resources blocked by the policy. Without reporting, security teams cannot detect attacks in progress or fix false positives that may break functionality.
security_hardening.currentRisk: CSP violations (potential XSS attempts) go undetected without reporting configured
security_hardening.remediation: Add CSP reporting directives: 1) 'report-uri /api/csp-report' for legacy browser support, 2) 'report-to csp-endpoint' for modern Reporting API, 3) Create a /api/csp-report endpoint that logs violations to your monitoring system (Datadog RUM is already integrated), 4) Use Report-Only mode first to test before enforcing new rules
